title: Characterize high-zoom workload before introducing desktop parallel rendering
changes: Reused the observed enemy replay at zoom 6 (570x322) for one ordinary and one detailed profile run; additional rows are not the dominant cost in this scenario. Keep parallel zoom and GPU policy unchanged.
validation: 3530-frame run with 120 warm-up frames: ordinary 7.623306 ms/frame, detailed 7.723037 ms/frame. Across 3410 profiled frames extra rows average 0.634410 ms (8.2161% of core), p99 total 9.389758 ms, max 10.063026 ms, no over-budget frames and no invalid stage samples.

Ordinary/profile initial and final state hashes, framebuffer and execution counts match. GUI zoom and reload worked, but Undo revealed the separately tracked restored-preview stride bug; driver exit alone was not treated as visual success.
limitations: One workload characterization and overhead estimate, not a five-pair speedup result, isolated AI measurement, hardware GPU benchmark or coverage of all aspect ratios and CPUs.
